Dear [Miss Cox](/person/1642)
I cannot promise to vote for [Anne Fay](/person/1679) but she interests me much, as I have seen a good deal of the same kind of illness and I will see whether it is possible.
I well remember the days of the Cardioscope, which I think was one of the best ideas [we](/periodical/52) ever had.[^1] I have now a [fellow Editor](/person/329) who has taken the MSS especially of poetry. I think she must have your verses

yours truly

C M Yonge


[^1]: ‘The Cardioscope’ was a series in MP (July-November 1851). The idea was that an instrument could test the feelings of the human heart as a stethoscope does. There is a volume of poems, 1887, by Agnes Cox. CMY is evidently being asked to cast a vote in favour of Anne Fay for admission to some hospital or almshouse. There is a probable contributor called [Harriet Lucy Cox](/person/375) (b. Waddesdon 1825/6) who later married the Rev. Arthur Baker (1817-1868) and transcribed books into Braille; it is possible that she may have been the author of ‘The Cardioscope’, and a relation of this Miss Cox.
